findings.title: Inverted lightness in embedded-post author color
findings.body: Line 291 is dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)) but the original was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%). The light-theme value changed from 30% to 70% and the dark-theme complement is backwards; consistent mapping elsewhere is 30% primary / 70% secondary. Consequence: light theme author links become much lighter/washed out and dark theme gets the wrong shade.

findings.title: Wrong lightness for group-member name
findings.body: Line 522 uses dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%)) but the diff shows the original was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%). The light-theme color is changed from 30% to 50% instead of preserving 30% with a 70% secondary complement. Consequence: light theme regresses to a lighter gray and dark theme mapping is incorrect.

findings.title: Wrong lightness for mobile group-member name
findings.body: Line 497 uses 50%/50% but the original was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%). Same error as desktop/user.scss: light value should stay 30% with secondary 70%. Consequence: unintended color change on light theme and wrong dark-theme color.

findings.title: Wrong lightness for mobile topic-map h3
findings.body: Line 182 uses dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%)) but the original was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%). The desktop equivalent correctly maps 20% to 20%/80%. Consequence: mobile light theme h3 becomes much lighter than intended and dark theme is wrong.

findings.title: Inverted lightness for custom-message-length
findings.body: Line 102 is dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%)) but the original was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%). The desktop modal correctly maps 70% to 70%/30%. Here light and dark values are swapped. Consequence: light theme text becomes much darker and dark theme much lighter than intended, likely unreadable.
